function: Excluded, above_phy (p. 3): the learned safety-RL (CUP) policy only sets user weights for rate scheduling across time slots; the precoders come from a classical WMMSE algorithm (pp. 6, 10).
notes: Reason above_phy. p. 3: the CUP agent derives "user weights (action) reflecting priority in user rate scheduling, rather than high-dimensional beamforming matrices". p. 1: "a safety reinforcement learning-based algorithm to optimize rate scheduling by allocating user weights, and a weighted minimum mean squared error (WMMSE) algorithm to solve the WSR maximization". p. 6: Section IV is "Data-Driven Safety-RL-Based User Weight Scheduling", and Algorithm 1 computes the precoders with the WMMSE of Algorithm 3 (p. 10), which has closed-form updates and no trained parameters. p. 11: the baselines EDF, MTF and equal weights are scheduling rules feeding the same WMMSE ("All schemes generate user weights as output to the WMMSE algorithm 3"), and the main metrics are delay jitter and delay violation ratio (p. 12). No physical-layer decision is learned, so it is not a joint physical-layer and scheduling design; no_learning not used because learning is the core of the method. Reviewer may check whether learned WSR user weights should count as learned precoding (area 3).
